title: Israeli Deputy Foreign Minister Warns Iran War Could Resume
description_short: Sharren Haskel warned on June 23, 2026 that war with Iran was very likely unless the Iranian regime changed.
description_medium: Israel’s Deputy Foreign Minister Sharren Haskel warned on June 23, 2026, that war with Iran was “very probable” unless there was “a huge change within the regime.” Her remarks followed a U.S.–Iran memorandum intended to extend a tenuous ceasefire. Reuters reported Israel was not part of the negotiations. The sources establish a warning about the deal’s fragility, not an Israeli decision to restart fighting or a promise to do so within days.
description_long: On June 23, 2026, Israel’s Deputy Foreign Minister Sharren Haskel told a Jerusalem press briefing attended by news.com.au that renewed war with Iran was “very probable” unless there was “a huge change within the regime.” She also said, “We are at a very dangerous point right now.” Her remarks came after the United States and Iran announced a memorandum intended to extend a tenuous ceasefire and open talks toward a permanent truce. Reuters reported that Israel had not participated in the negotiations and that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had distanced Israel from the agreement, leaving uncertainty about whether the ceasefire would hold. The reporting supports a warning about the fragile agreement, not evidence that Israel had decided to restart fighting or promised to do so within days. The frozen record’s claims about unnamed officials, Iranian provocations, and weaknesses in Trump’s framework are not established by the accessed reports and are omitted. Its Associated Press link concerns a separate Gaza dispute and does not support this Iran entry.

title: Federal COVID Vaccine and Test Access Had Separate Timelines
description_short: The vaccine-access program ended in August 2024; federal COVID test ordering continued into 2025.
description_medium: The CDC says its Bridge Access Program for uninsured and underinsured adults ended in August 2024 after updated vaccines replaced the prior doses. Reuters reported that the Trump administration reversed a planned shutdown of COVIDtests.gov in February 2025. CNN reported that the site was not accepting new orders on March 10, while noting that a permanent shutdown was unclear. These records do not support one January 20 action ending all free vaccines and tests.
description_long: CDC records show that the Bridge Access Program provided free COVID-19 vaccines to adults without insurance or whose plans did not cover the full cost. After the FDA authorized updated 2024–25 vaccines on August 22, 2024, the earlier doses could no longer be administered and CDC said the program had ended. That was before the second Trump administration. The federal at-home test program followed a different timeline: Reuters reported that the administration reversed a planned February 2025 shutdown of COVIDtests.gov, which shipped free tests to households. On March 10, CNN reported the site was not accepting new orders, but said it was unclear whether the program had shut down permanently. These separate records do not support the frozen entry’s assertion that one January 20 decision ended all free vaccine and test programs. The accessed sources also do not establish that all CDC mitigation guidance was removed, that federal test stockpiles were allowed to expire, or that the country had no federal response mechanism. Those claims are excluded pending specific evidence.
